questions.question: Which license requires derivative works to remain open-source (copyleft)?
questions.explanation: The GPL's copyleft clause requires modified versions to be distributed under the same open-source license.

questions.question: What executes code line by line without compilation?
What software runs on a server and is accessed via browser?
questions.explanation: Web apps require no local installation.

questions.question: What environment allows running code without affecting the main system?
What type of software can be tried before purchasing?
What manages software updates and installations?
What software layer sits between OS and applications?
What detects and fixes software bugs?
questions.explanation: Debuggers help find and resolve errors.

questions.question: What software development model releases frequent updates?
What interface allows programs to communicate?
Practice of merging code changes into a shared repository many times a day.
questions.explanation: CI has developers merge and build frequently so conflicts surface early.

questions.question: Automated tests that verify individual functions or small units of code.
questions.explanation: Unit tests check isolated pieces of code and run fast in the build pipeline.

questions.question: Distributed version control system created by Linus Torvalds.
questions.explanation: Git tracks code history and lets teams branch and merge work.

questions.question: Tool that scans source code for style issues and suspicious patterns.
questions.explanation: Linters flag style violations and likely bugs before code is even run.

questions.question: Pre-release testing phase where real users try the software.
questions.explanation: Beta releases expose the software to real-world use before final launch.
